Proposed link from neuronal TRIM8 mislocalization to intellectual disability; intermediate steps unknown.

Podocyte injury produces the segmental sclerosing glomerular lesion. None of the cited TRIM8 sources states this step in this direction, so the edge carries no evidence of its own; the foot process fusion cited on the node is the observed injury.
Loss of the podocyte filtration barrier allows protein to leak into the urine. No cited TRIM8 source states this step directly, so the edge carries no evidence of its own.

nodes.description: Heterozygous nonsense and frameshift variants in the final exon of TRIM8 truncate the protein between residues 390 and 487. Because they lie in the last exon the transcripts escape nonsense-mediated decay, so a truncated protein lacking the C-terminal region is expected to be made. TRIM8 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase; ClinGen records that these variants are hypothesized to act through gain-of-function or toxic effects, while patient kidney tissue shows loss of detectable TRIM8 and accumulation of its ubiquitination target SOCS1. The direction of the change in ligase activity is therefore recorded as abnormal rather than decreased or increased.

nodes.description: Wild-type TRIM8 forms nuclear bodies that frequently abut Gemini and Cajal bodies; truncated patient variants instead spread diffusely through the nucleoplasm in podocytes and neuronal cells. The study proposing this mechanism links it to both the kidney and brain disease. A 2025 preprint describes the bodies as condensates formed by the C-terminal disordered region and links their disruption to altered proteasomal regulation, TAK1/NF-kB signaling and podocyte dysfunction; this has not yet been peer reviewed, and no neuronal mechanism has been shown.
